subject: ouroboros
title: CI-blocking size ratchet: 1600-line module / 300-line function ceilings with tracked debt, enforced in every job
evidence: ouroboros/review.py:19-23 (MAX_MODULE_LINES=1600, MAX_FUNCTION_LINES=300, MAX_MODULE_BYTES=200_000); .github/workflows/ci.yml:175,293 (pytest -m size_ratchet in each tier); tests/test_size_ratchet_ci_shape.py:17 (every CI job must run the lane); tests/test_size_headroom.py:12-40 (headroom incl. zero/negative surfaced to health)
one_why: Anti-god-file discipline is mechanized rather than cultural -- the mechanism a self-modifying agent needs so its own rewrites cannot bloat past reviewable size; any agent repo can adopt the ratchet+debt-registration shape.

subject: ouroboros
title: AST analysis of inline interpreter code in shell commands resolves write targets, with fail-closed scoped to where danger exists
evidence: ouroboros/tools/shell_guards.py:376 (_python_write_targets_and_unknown), :361 (opaque-call detection), :1447-1480 (_dynamic_write_could_hit_repo: unresolved target blocks only if code names a repo path or cwd is inside repo -- 'Fail-closed is right where the danger exists, not everywhere')
one_why: Goes past regex deny-lists: python -c bodies are parsed for open()/write spellings and only genuinely-unresolvable targets near the protected root are refused, so false-blocks on external deliverables stopped driving whack-a-mole (comment at :1462).

subject: ouroboros
title: Closed profile x resource-root x operation matrix as the single tool-access SSOT, summarized back to parent and child at schedule time
evidence: ouroboros/tool_access_types.py:18-56 (6 profiles x 9 roots x 10 operations Literal vocabulary + _POLICY), ouroboros/tool_access.py:195 (decide_tool_access single seam), :88-117 (summarize_subagent_profile derives child capability from the same matrix to prevent wasted blocked rounds)
one_why: The vocabulary is closed and the matrix is one table -- visibility/residency is explicitly separated from authority ('Residency never grants execution authority', tool_policy.py:1-5), which is the separation most approval-gate agents lack.

subject: ouroboros
title: Append-only byte-prefix transcript invariant: compaction seams stamp a sanction, every other cache break is counted in usage
evidence: ouroboros/transcript_prefix.py:1-16 (invariant + OpenAI-family byte-prefix cache rationale, issue #906 'measured 2026-09-14'), :32 (sanction_rewrite), ouroboros/loop.py:337-355 (_record_transcript_prefix counts prompt_prefix_breaks per unsanctioned break; 'records and never blocks a send')
one_why: Seeded id observed with its strongest mechanism yet: cache monotonicity is a named invariant with sanctioned exceptions AND a per-task counter that makes cache loss a visible, budgetable cost rather than an invisible bill.

subject: ouroboros
title: Live-model lanes wired into CI: nightly paid E2E stand with explicit $30 cap and honest skip, plus real-provider skill-review smoke at $1.2/run
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:9,71 (cron 03:17 paid e2e_live stand, skipped honestly without key), :67 (dispatch input '$30 cap'), :631,657-660 (attempt-reserve math proving the cap arithmetic), :385-456 (skill_smoke live installs + review->grant->enable flow on a cheap reviewer model, split into two pytest processes so only one holds the API key)
one_why: First subject observed past the verification-8 ceiling noted for codex/cline/pi: real models run in CI on a schedule with an enforced money bound; still no scored benchmark gate or fuzzing, which keeps it 9 not 10.

subject: ouroboros
title: Stdlib mock OpenAI-compatible server on 127.0.0.1 drives whole-loop tests, backed by a provider contract catalog
evidence: tests/fixtures_mock_llm.py:16-54 (MockLLMServer ThreadingHTTPServer, /v1/chat/completions, hold/release knob so a browser fixture can keep a task inside its first model call), tests/provider_contract_catalog.py, tests/provider_contract_ci.py
one_why: Zero-dependency faux provider that tests real HTTP transport and concurrency, not just client stubs -- the hold/release trick makes mid-first-call UI states testable.

subject: ouroboros
title: In-loop resume journals restore round index, route, and tool schemas; stale snapshots cannot revive a spent wait
evidence: ouroboros/loop.py:387-420 (load_owner_wait/load_budget_pause restore model/effort/round_idx/tool_schemas; unanswered tool calls closed as execution-unknown WITHOUT replay), ouroboros/owner_wait.py:207-217 (resume refused unless status non-terminal, state=='waiting', and wait_id matches)
one_why: Resume semantics at loop granularity (not session granularity): a paid-but-unanswered model call is treated as an unknown outcome that is closed, never resent -- the resend-honesty discipline most resume designs skip.

subject: ouroboros
title: Delivery acceptance panel: host-forced review with a closed set of typed reasons, per-root paid review-cycle ceiling, and identical-diff refusal
evidence: ouroboros/loop.py:113-119 (closed typed acceptance reasons -- 'none derives from model prose'; unspecified is fail-closed), loop.py:571-574 (acceptance observation + transcript seal before send), ouroboros/tools/commit_gate.py:1-27 (advisory-freshness gate, durable commit-attempt record, free identical-diff refusal, per-root-task paid max-review-cycles, review-contract fingerprint)
one_why: Finish-gate taken to its adversarial extreme: a reviewer model must accept the delivery, the reason vocabulary is host-computed so the model cannot author its own bypass, and money spent on review cycles is capped per root task.

subject: ouroboros
title: Runtime-mode tiers gate which source surfaces the agent may rewrite, with consent-tested elevation and constitution-protected files
evidence: ouroboros/runtime_mode_policy.py:1-6 (advanced may evolve app layer but not core contracts/safety files; pro through triad+scope review), :47+ (argv predicate refusing BIBLE.md deletion and git history rewrites), BIBLE.md:7-14 (constitutional amendment requires reviewed release outside Cyber Pro), tests/test_runtime_mode_elevation.py:87-147 (elevation refused without consent flag, downgrade allowed)
one_why: Self-modification with an enforced protected core: the ladder from ordinary task -> app-layer evolution -> core evolution -> unrestricted agency is code, consent-gated, and test-proven -- no other subject in the corpus models who-may-edit-what at this granularity.

subject: ouroboros
title: No OS-level boundary anywhere; elevated cyber_pro makes internal permission/review checks advisory-only
evidence: grep seatbelt/bwrap/seccomp across ouroboros+supervisor hits only ouroboros/config.py:233-241 (delegated containment mechanism is macOS-only per Claudexor docs; a run reporting no mechanism is DISCLOSED, not refused -- 'Disclose instead of forbid'); ouroboros/runtime_mode_policy.py:33-41 (mode_has_unrestricted_agency: internal mechanisms lose veto authority in cyber_pro)
one_why: In-process policy plus AST guards cannot contain a process that can edit the policy at elevated modes; the honesty about the gap (SECURITY.md names the boundary surfaces for reporters) is exemplary, but the boundary itself is absent off-macOS -- this is what caps safety-enforcement at 6.

subject: ouroboros
title: Refactor leaves preserve ~150-name historical re-export facades because tests and sibling leaves monkeypatch private names through them
evidence: ouroboros/loop.py:686-886 ('Cohesive leaves own the implementations... Keep the full re-export surface: production callers and tests address these historical loop bindings'); ouroboros/tool_access.py:31-34 ('extracted VERBATIM... so historical imports and monkeypatch targets keep working'); ~40 'noqa: F401 -- historical facade surface' import markers across the two files
one_why: The size ratchet keeps files small but the extraction seams are frozen by test coupling: leaf-to-leaf calls resolve through the facade at call time, so the module graph the reader sees is not the dependency graph the code runs -- a cautionary pattern for any refactor-under-tests program.

subject: ouroboros
title: Background consciousness wake: model-chosen next-interval inside owner bounds, rolling-24h cost allowance, exponential backoff, explicit no-re-arm events
evidence: ouroboros/consciousness.py:1-30 (tick order with typed outcomes; unreadable allowance ledger is a disclosed skip 'allowance_unknown', never a silent block; launched wake inherits the day's remaining allowance as its graceful cost ceiling; failures double the interval up to max; owner messages and wake finishes never re-arm), consciousness_allowance.py, consciousness_wake.py
one_why: Autonomous periodic agency budgeted like a wallet: the interval is the model's choice within owner clamps, the day's remaining money is the wake's ceiling so it never dies mid-first-call, and unknown ledger state fails disclosed rather than silently blocking or spending.
